.qc-cache/coldwater-strict-2026-10-07-v14-quick/task/environment/instructions/ (listing: behaviour.md, integration.md, overview.md, policy.md, security.md, ui.md - six notes, matching 'the six notes')
evidence: Read cold, task/instruction.md is three first-person prose paragraphs with no numbered acceptance list, no shall/must table, no feature matrix and no framework/file-layout/endpoint recipe (the defects named in quality-checks.md:11). Line 1 states a personal motive and workflow: "I'd like a small local playground for working on JavaScript and complete HTML files... I often paste a long one-line experiment, format it, make changes in several places, and then run it beside the source. I want to keep the versions that work without losing a draft when another tab saves first." Line 3 defers detail to the notes in natural terms ("Please read the six notes in /instructions before building"); the six notes exist. Line 5 gives only the minimal runtime contract (/app, serve at /, node /app/server.js, /app/app.db, no sign-in), phrased as how the person starts and uses it ("I start it with...", "I should be able to open it..."), which is the deliverable contract required by row 4, not a build recipe. The newly appended sentence, "Before you hand it over, please check it yourself the way I'll use it: type into the editor, run the code and save a snippet, and make sure nothing breaks.", is a conversational hand-off request in the requester's own voice ("the way I'll use it"); its three verbs are a short inline prose clause, not an enumerated acceptance checklist, and it names no test framework, command, endpoint or file. It does not convert the ask into a spec sheet. Counter-scenarios tried: (a) a spec-like instruction that would fail - e.g. the sentence rewritten as '1. Type in editor 2. Run 3. Save snippet; all must pass' or adding 'use Playwright to assert...' - is not what is present; (b) a conforming builder is not disadvantaged by the sentence since it adds no hidden product requirement (typing, running and saving snippets are already the core product named in lines 1-3). No runtime evidence is needed for this text-only row.
